summary: Gilam Seok is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at Hankuk University of Foreign Studies and a doctorate at Dongguk University WISE Campus. He held posts at Dongguk University WISE Campus and Geumgang University.

Gilbert Lazard (1920–2018) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1940. He served at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1980) and the University of Paris (~1958–1980).

Gilbert Slater (1864–1938) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning a doctorate from the London School of Economics, he served as Principal of Ruskin College (1909–1915) and became the first Professor of Indian Economics at the University of Madras (1915).

Gilbert Zhe Chen is a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Washington University in St. Louis (2012–2019) and was appointed Associate Professor at Towson University in 2019.

Gilberte de Coral-Rémusat (1903–1943) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She studied at the École du Louvre and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jean Przyluski, Paul Pelliot, and Paul Masson-Oursel.

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at the CNRS, a member of EHESS, and an exchange program director at FMSH.

Gillian R. Hart (1934–2004) was a linguistics and Indology scholar. She studied at Reading, Lady Margaret Hall, and Oxford under Thomas Burrow, later lecturing in Classics at Aberystwyth (1960–1969) and at Durham University (1969–1993).
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin, attested in 2008.

Giorgio Renato Franci (1933–2012) was an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Bologna under Luigi Heilmann (~1952–1956) and later held an academic post there (~1964–2005).

Philosopher Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) studied at Pisa and Florence. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Sapienza University of Rome, and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and the Royal Academy of Italy.

Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. After doctoral studies at Genoa and further study at Florence, he lectured at Florence (1910) and held teaching posts and a chair at Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

Giovanni Verardi is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur. He held posts at Ca' Foscari, Bologna, and L'Orientale, with visiting professorships at Collège de France, Seijo, Kyoto, and ICPBS.

Girijesh Dhar Dwivedi is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned an Acharya master's degree in Sanskrit from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (2010–2011) and pursued a PhD at SunRise University (2019–2026).

Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) studied at Presidency University, Calcutta Medical College, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

Girolamo Donati (1857–1901) was an Indologist who studied under Angelo De Gubernatis. He succeeded De Gubernatis in 1890, serving as libero docente of Sanskrit at the University of Florence (~1888–1901) and as conservator at the Museo Indiano.

Gisbert Combaz (1869–1941) was a sinologist and art historian who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles and under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He taught at Ixelles, Université Nouvelle de Bruxelles, and the Académie Royale des Beaux-Arts.

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the Universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2003, she was attested as a research fellow at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisela Freund (1920–2023) was an archaeologist. She studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague (~1939–1944) and later served as Head of the Department of Prehistory at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1969–1987).

Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and at Kyushu. He held professorships at Peking and Koyasan Universities, serving multiple terms as president of Koyasan University.
Giti Dutt is an archaeologist and researcher who, as attested in 2026, pursued a PhD at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron.
